findings.issue: Referential integrity does not check sequences[].participants[].zone. The model schema (schema/archmap-model.schema.json participant.zone, design section 5 participants[{..., zone, node?}]) makes it a zone id, but checkIntegrity only resolves participant.node (line 133). A dangling participant zone validates clean. P1.2's description lists only 'sequence participant node', so this is a gap in the spec as well as the code, not a contradiction of a task clause.
findings.resolution: Add ref(zones, p.zone, `/sequences/${i}/participants/${j}/zone`, 'zone') beside the node check, with a case in tests/validate.test.mjs and a golden-model run to confirm every participant zone in tests/fixtures/golden/architecture.model.json resolves (a script run found none dangling).

findings.issue: tests/schema.test.mjs carries its own second JSON Schema interpreter (check) alongside scripts/lib/jsonschema.mjs, added one task later. s5, s7, s8, s9, s10, s11 and s12 assert schema behaviour through the test's copy, not through the interpreter validate.mjs ships. The two can drift: for example check() on an unknown type throws a TypeError where validateSchema throws a clear error, and check() ignores $ref inside oneOf the same way only by coincidence. A schema change that the shipped interpreter rejects could still pass these tests.
findings.resolution: Replace check() with validateSchema from scripts/lib/jsonschema.mjs (error list is empty means valid), so the schema tests exercise the interpreter the validator uses. The keyword-subset walk (KEYWORDS) can stay.
